01 · Welcome
Welcome to Troopod, Vestwell.
This document is your single source of truth for this engagement: scope, process, timelines, and next steps, all in one place. Troopod is a website performance and CRO partner. Vestwell is the modern savings platform.
Where vestwell.com stands today
Average mobile Performance score across the 492 pages we tested.
Desktop average: 59.
Why we're here
We tested 492 pages: every URL in your sitemap, plus the Resources pages found on the site. A third of pages score below 50 on mobile, and in Google's mobile test a page takes about 9 seconds on average to show its main content. We checked the measurements against your source code and found the specific causes. Every fix is made in the website's own code, and Google Tag Manager and all tracking stay exactly as they are.
This engagement starts with page speed, the foundation. On top of it we add the technical SEO and AEO layer, so search engines and AI tools can load and read every page correctly.
Please note
Scores move from test to test. A single PageSpeed run can vary by 5–8 points, so we measure targets as the average of 5 runs, mobile and desktop, on an agreed list of URLs.
Targets apply to the tracking setup at sign-off. New tags, pixels, or widgets added later will lower the score, so please flag them before they go live.
Targets cover the key templates. Home, product, audience, blog, and news pages. Resources pages improve too, but are reported separately because Google's test often times out on them today.
Targets assume the reviewed code is what's live. The source code we work on must match your live production branch.

Common questions
Will the design of the site change?
No. We only work on code, scripts, assets, and page tags. The site looks exactly the same and loads faster.
How will we know what changed?
You get a PageSpeed before/after report using the same method as the baseline, plus a list of every fix that shipped.
How does this help the AEO metrics we track?
It gives every page a fast, correctly tagged base for your content and PR work to build on. Section 13 shows how each fix connects to each metric.
Will this affect our tracking or marketing tags?
No. Google Tag Manager and every marketing and tracking tag stay exactly as they are today. All fixes are made in the website's own code, so analytics, ads, and conversion tracking keep working as before.
Can anything break?
Every change goes to staging first. Before each release we run a regression checklist: forms and demo booking, cookie banner, navigation and menus, page transitions, Sanity preview and visual editing, and every page template on mobile and desktop. The hero keeps the same animation; only the way it starts changes. Releases are small and separate, so any issue can be traced to one change and rolled back in minutes.
Who writes the new page titles and descriptions?
We build the system: every page gets its own title and description, with automatic fallbacks so nothing is ever blank. Custom wording stays with your team, editable in Sanity.

What's slowing the site down
Each cause was found in Lighthouse diagnostics and then confirmed in your source code.
#IssueWhat we foundAffectsIn this engagement
1Hero content hidden until JavaScript loadsThe main heading and image can't appear until React has loaded, adding a 2–4s delayLCPFixed
2Resources pages load the whole libraryEach topic page loads the entire Resources library (about 1.6 MB) and filters it in the browserLCP, TBT, CLSFixed
3Background downloadsEvery internal link prefetches large data files (about 4.6 MB on one blog page)LCP, TBTFixed
4Page data sent twiceThe same page data is sent twice, plus 142 KB of menu data on every pageTBTPartly: duplicate removed
5Too many priority imagesSeveral images are marked high priority and compete for bandwidthLCPFixed
6Slow server responseNetlify forwards page requests instead of serving them from the edge, adding 100–400msFCP, LCPFixed
7Layout shiftDynamic grids and a late-loading banner shift the layout: up to 0.75 on Resources pages, 0.15 on the homepageCLSFixed
8Page transitions, CSS, and fontsA page-transition library loads on every page, plus 10–11 render-blocking stylesheets and large display fontsTBT, FCPSeparate scope
Left unchanged by agreement: Google Tag Manager
GTM and its tags (GA4, Google Ads, Facebook, LinkedIn, Reddit, Clarity, CookieYes) use about 1–1.2s of main-thread time on each page. They stay exactly as they are, so tracking and attribution are never at risk.
Already optimised in your code
GSAP, smooth scrolling, and HubSpot already load late. Images already use AVIF and WebP. Fonts already use font-display: swap.

Conditions for the targets
  • Measurement: average of 5 PageSpeed runs, mobile and desktop, on an agreed list of URLs, using lab data. A single run can vary by 5–8 points.
  • Scope: key templates (home, product, audience, blog, news). Resources pages improve significantly but are reported separately, as Lighthouse often times out on them today.
  • Tags frozen: targets apply to the GTM setup at sign-off. New tags, pixels, or widgets added later will lower the score.
  • Production code: the reviewed source code must match the live production branch.
  • Google changes: results are measured against the Lighthouse version in use at the time of the audit.
  • Content: very large new images, videos, or embeds added in the CMS can lower scores on those pages.

  • A base your team can build on. Every page your content and PR teams publish lands on a fast, readable site.

Background downloads of other pages
Every link on a page quietly downloaded data for the page it pointed to.
Turned off background prefetching in the shared link component.68 → 2 background downloads (homepage)
Page data sent twice
Each page’s content was included twice in the code sent to the browser.
The content is now sent once.Homepage data ~380 KB → 140 KB
Too many images marked “load first”
Several images competed for top priority with the main hero image.
Only the main hero image (and the first blog card) is marked to load first.3 → 1 priority image (homepage)
Layout moving while loading
Some blocks appeared late and pushed content around.
Space is reserved for these blocks before they load.Homepage mobile layout shift 0.101 → 0.009
Article dates caused pages to rebuild
Post dates were shown in the visitor’s time zone, so some visitors’ browsers rebuilt the whole page.
Dates now display the same for every visitor.0 page errors across US, UTC and India time zones
None of these changes touch tracking, design, or content. Each one is a separate change that can be reviewed and reversed on its own.
